provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Science is asking why
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to ask questions about things they see.
The pupils should be able to identify science tools.
Introduction:
We see many things every day. We can ask why they happen.
Content:
Science is asking why things happen. We use tools to help us find answers. Our tools include magnifying glass and thermometer. We can use these to look closely and measure.
Class activity:
Question wall. Pupils write questions on sticky notes and stick on the wall.
Evaluation questions:
What is science?
Name one science tool.
What question did you ask today?
Summary:
Science helps us understand the world by asking questions.

topics.title: Measure it
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use a ruler to measure length.
The pupils should be able to identify different measuring tools.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about science tools. Today we learn how to measure things.
Content:
We measure length with rulers. We measure weight with scales. We measure how much with cups. We can measure our books and tables. We can measure water in jugs.
Class activity:
Measure everything hunt. Pupils find objects in class and measure them with rulers.
Evaluation questions:
Name one measuring tool.
How long is your book?
What do we use to measure weight?
Summary:
Measuring helps us know how big or heavy things are.

topics.title: Magnets at work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify magnetic materials.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate attraction and repulsion.
Introduction:
We have used rulers and scales. Today we learn about magnets that pull things.
Content:
Magnets can pull some things. This is called attraction. Magnets push other magnets away. This is called repulsion. Iron objects stick to magnets. Paper and plastic do not stick.
Class activity:
Magnetic maze game. Pupils move a magnet under paper to move a paperclip through a maze.
Evaluation questions:
What can magnets pull?
What is it called when magnets push away?
Which object sticks to a magnet?
Summary:
Magnets can pull some things and push others away.

topics.title: Electric basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify basic electric parts.
The pupils should be able to make a simple circuit.
Introduction:
Last week we played with magnets. Today we learn about making light with electricity.
Content:
Electricity makes bulbs light up. We need a battery to make electricity. We need wires to carry electricity. When we connect them, the bulb lights up. This is called a circuit.
Class activity:
Light the bulb with help. Pupils connect battery, bulb and wire with teacher help.
Evaluation questions:
What makes a bulb light up?
What do we need for electricity?
What is a circuit?
Summary:
Electricity travels through wires to light bulbs.

topics.title: Static fun
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create static electricity.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate static effects.
Introduction:
We learned about electric circuits. Today we learn about static electricity.
Content:
Static electricity is when electricity stays still. We can make it by rubbing a balloon on our hair. The balloon can pick up small paper bits. This is static electricity at work.
Class activity:
Sparkly static experiments. Pupubs rub balloons on hair and pick up paper bits.
Evaluation questions:
How do we make static electricity?
What happens when we rub a balloon?
What can static electricity do?
Summary:
Static electricity can make things stick together.

topics.title: Sink and float deep dive
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to predict if objects will sink or float.
The pupils should be able to explain why ships float.
Introduction:
We played with static electricity. Today we learn about things that sink and float.
Content:
Some things sink in water. Some things float. Heavy ships float because they are wide. Wide things float better than thin things. Clay sinks but clay boats float.
Class activity:
Clay boat challenge. Pupils make boats from clay and see if they float.
Evaluation questions:
What happens to heavy ships in water?
Why do clay boats float?
What sinks in water?
Summary:
Things float when they are wide and light.

topics.title: Air power
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate air movement.
The pupils should be able to make a simple air toy.
Introduction:\ Last week we learned about sinking and floating. Today we learn about air power.
Content:
Air is all around us. We cannot see it but we can feel it. Air pushes things when it moves. We can use air to make rockets fly and parachutes fall slowly.
Class activity:
Straw rockets and parachutes. Pupils make paper rockets blow through straws and mini parachutes.
Evaluation questions:
What is air power?
How do rockets move with air?
What makes parachutes fall slowly?
Summary:
Air can push things and make them move.

topics.title: Water cycle start
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify parts of the water cycle.
The pupils should be able to explain evaporation.
Introduction:
We learned about air power. Today we learn how water moves in the air.
Content:
Water from puddles goes up to the air. This is called evaporation. The water makes clouds. When clouds are heavy, water falls as rain. This is called rain.
Class activity:
Watch and draw. Pupils watch water evaporate from a cup and draw the water cycle.
Evaluation questions:
What is evaporation?
Where does rain come from?
What happens to puddles on sunny days?
Summary:
Water goes from ground to air and back again.

topics.title: Recycling science
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sort recyclable materials.
The pupils should be able to name one recycled item.
Introduction:
We learned about the water cycle. Today we learn about reusing materials.
Content:
Recycling means using things again. We can sort paper, plastic and metal. These can be made into new things. Bottle banks collect plastic bottles for recycling.
Class activity:
Bottle bank craft. Pupils make craft items from recycled plastic bottles.
Evaluation questions:
What is recycling?
Name one recyclable material.
What can we make from recycled bottles?
Summary:
Recycling helps us use materials again.

topics.title: Revision and inventor day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate one experiment learned.
The pupils should be able to explain an experiment like a scientist.
Introduction:
This week we revise all we learned about science.
Content:
We learned about magnets, electricity, sinking and floating. We learned about air and water. We can show our favorite experiment to friends.
Class activity:
Show my experiment. Pupils demonstrate one experiment to the class.
Evaluation questions:
What is your favorite science experiment?
How do you make a bulb light up?
Why do ships float?
Summary:
We are all scientists when we ask why and try things.
